$note: Rules changes the sim tested, in order (sim/economy.mjs applies them one by one and re-runs). Every 'after' must equal rules/fieldworks.json; a null 'before' means the key did not exist.

changes.why: With 78 attackers today the upper clamp held the blight on 26 of 60 days, so a close did not visibly move it; at 2 the upper clamp binds on no day, though the lower clamp still holds the thin early weeks (step 8) and a filling map squeezes it (step 7).
One machine per attacker made a night 80+ machines on the real backlog; a quarter keeps the backlog legible in the wave without swamping it.
The performance budget (GDD §3.3) is 40 machines on a phone; the wave never exceeds it.
Under the real-day clock (D25) the day count grows without end; the day term stops growing after a week, so night 60 is not three times night 20.
At 100 the Keeper reached level 10 on day 43, about a level every four days; at 200 level 5 lands on day 18 and level 10 is projected for day 90, the quarter.

On the real pace the stated lessons alone bought seven pylons a week and the map's free ground ran out on day 15 (day 17 after steps 1–5), after which the blight could no longer show the backlog. A pylon at 8 cells is two lesson days; a median day still funds a turret and a habitat (4 cells).

With the cost doubled the map still filled by day 22. A shorter reach makes each pylon about 4 new tiles, so half the ground (the run's win, D30) arrives around day 30 and the free ground lasts to day 51.

Counted honestly, the lower clamp held the blight on 13 of the early days, when only a handful of orders were old enough to attack, so a close there moved nothing. At 8 the floor still draws a thin edge of blight and the blight follows the backlog on 49 of 60 days.
